subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novahealth.ai>, Emily Zhou <emily@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks for taking the time today — good session. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our discussion with your infra and product teams:

1) Targets you called out
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 150 ms at P50 for single-shot generation (primary).
- Sustained throughput: ~300 requests/sec for your peak traffic profile.
- Concurrency: up to 50 concurrent streaming clients during peak windows.
- Streaming behavior: SSE (preferred) but WebSocket supported — need chunk cadence ~100–200 ms for progressive UX (no large 1s+ gaps).

2) Items we need from your side
- Representative traffic profile (payload size distribution, tokens-in, tokens-out).
- Typical prompt complexity (system + user tokens), any large-context sessions.
- Any model constraints (open model family / required safety filters).

I've attached a sample_traffic.csv template you can drop data into. If you can send that by EOW, engineering can size a PoC cluster and run a controlled TTFT/streaming cadence test.

3) Redwood PoC proposal (high-level)
- 2-week PoC: dedicated test cluster with identical model variant to prod, synthetic and replayed traffic runs.
- Measurement: TTFT (P50/P90/P99), first-byte cadence, per-chunk latency distribution, and end-to-end UX (SSE/WebSocket).
- Success criteria: P50 TTFT <= 150 ms; P90 TTFT <= 300 ms; no chunk gap > 400 ms for >99% of streaming requests under target throughput.

Next steps
- Can you share the sample_traffic.csv and one engineering contact for network/egress testing?
- Proposed follow-up: quick sync Wed 3/3 at 10am PT to finalize PoC scope.

Thanks — happy to adjust targets if your product team wants a different TTFT cadence.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

redwood.com | (650) 555-0119

From: Samir Patel <samir@novahealth.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhou <emily@novahealth.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Aditya — that recap matches our notes. A few clarifications from my side:

- TTFT target: 150 ms P50 is what product wants; engineering asked if you measure TTFT from request accept (post-auth) or from client TCP connect. We prefer request-accept as long as you document measurement points.
- Streaming: SSE is our preference. Chunk cadence of 100ms is ideal for the consumer UX team; if you can guarantee <=200ms, that is acceptable.
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent streaming clients is a ballpark for peak; sustained is closer to 25.

I've attached a filled sample_traffic.csv with a week's worth of sampled traffic patterns and typical payload sizes. Also included a short note from our infra lead (Emily) about our NAT gateway throughput and egress constraints.

One ask: please include an example of how Redwood reports per-chunk timing in the PoC deliverable (e.g., CSV or JSON output we can ingest).

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product
NovaHealth

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap and next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attached traffic sample — that's exactly what we need. A few answers and the PoC plan attached:

- Measurement point: we measure TTFT from request accept (post-auth) by default in our reporting. We'll include both client-observed and server-observed timestamps in the deliverable so you can reconcile.
- Per-chunk timing: our test harness will emit a per-chunk timing report (CSV) with fields: request_id, chunk_index, chunk_sent_ts, server_processing_ms, network_gap_ms. We'll include a sample in the PoC plan.
- Egress estimate: based on your traffic sample, expected outbound egress is ~1.2 Gbps during peak synthetic replay. We will put this in the PoC runbook so you can provision NAT capacity.

Attached is redwood_poc-plan.pdf — high-level test matrix, timeline, and roles. Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (alignment): finalize scope and sign test addendum (DocuSign link below).
- Week 1 (setup): bring up dedicated PoC cluster, baseline synthetic runs.
- Week 2 (validation): run replay tests and incremental load to target throughput, produce per-chunk timing reports and TTFT distributions.

DocuSign (test addendum): https://docusign.com/s/abcd-Redwood-PoC

Do Wed 3/3 10am PT still work for you? We'll bring Marissa (engineer) to walk through the measurement plan.

Best,
Aditya Rao
